summary: Geshe Lhakdor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery. He served at Tibet House, New Delhi, and became Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

Geshe Lhundub Sopa was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Gaden Chokor and Sera Jey under Lhundrub Thabkhe, Geshe Ngawang Rigsal, Geshe Ngawang Gendun, and Lhundrub Tsöndrü. He was Assistant Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1967–1997).

Geshe Lobsang Choedar works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 2010, he was attested as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics and held a post at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Lobsang Tenzin studied at Drepung Monastery. He served as Principal of the Central School for Tibetans, Principal and Director at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Chancellor of Sanchi University of Buddhist-Indic Studies.

Geshe Lobsang Tharchin (1921–2004) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery, where he earned his Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and also studied at Gyume Tantric Monastery.

Geshe Ngawang Nyima (1907–1990) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He held posts at Leiden University in 1960 and at Drepung Monastery (attested 1966 and 1995), serving as Geshe of sGo-mang sgrva-tshang.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Geshe Ngawang Samten studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Ganden Shartse Monastery. He was Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1988–2021) and held several visiting professorships.

Geshe Palden Drakpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and was attested as Librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi (1987–1992, 2004).

Geshe Rabten (1920–1986) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Trijang Rinpoche (~1945–1981), later teaching at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1964–1969).

Geshe Sonam Rinchen (1933–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. In 1978, he became a resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

Geshe Tashi Tsering is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery, Gyuto Monastery, and under Geshe Thubten Rinchen. His posts include teaching at Kopan Monastery, Gandhi Foundation College, and Jamyang Buddhist Centre (1994).

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Tenzin Dhargye studied under Ling Rinpoche and at Sera and Gyume monasteries. He held teaching posts at Sera and Gyume, taught at the University of Virginia, and became Director of Tibet Center Austria (2008).
Geshe Tshondru Kongpel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned Geshe degrees through his studies at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, where he was attested in 1991 and from 2001 to 2019.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden (1926–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery and under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Lodrö Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche. He served as a teacher of Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin completed his studies under Tenzin Gyatso, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki (1875–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and at Otani University. He spent his career at Otani University as a lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

Gherardo Gnoli (1937–2012) studied at the University of Rome and worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He taught at the University of Naples and University of Rome, and served as President of IsMEO and IsIAO.

Ghulam Yazdani (1885–1962), a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Aligarh Muslim University under Mohammad Ishaq and Nazir Ahmad. He taught at St. Stephen's, Rajshahi, and Government College Lahore before directing archaeology for Hyderabad State (~1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Rome under Raniero Gnoli, and began teaching at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" around 1992.
